_note: short_name/field are the NASA GES DISC / LP DAAC product and variable names to fetch. Verify each against the archive when running scripts/build_cache.py. 'scale' and 'offset' convert raw values to display_unit.

T2M.label: Air temperature (2 m)
T2M.definition: How warm the air is about 2 metres above the ground, the height where weather stations measure it. It is a reanalysis value: a weather model constrained by many satellite and ground observations.
T2M.why_it_matters: The most direct indicator of warming, and the baseline for almost every other change.

PRECIP.label: Precipitation (satellite)
PRECIP.definition: Rain and snow reaching the ground, estimated by combining many satellite microwave and infrared measurements. Reported here as the average daily amount for each month.
PRECIP.why_it_matters: Shows wetting or drying, which drives drought, floods, crops and water supply.

PRECTOT.label: Precipitation (model)
PRECTOT.definition: Total precipitation as simulated by the MERRA-2 reanalysis. Its main advantage over the satellite product is length: it starts in 1980, so it gives a much longer record.
PRECTOT.why_it_matters: A longer record makes trends easier to detect and to call significant.

AOD.label: Aerosol optical depth
AOD.definition: How much sunlight is blocked by haze, smoke, dust and pollution particles in the air above a place. 0 is perfectly clear. Values above about 0.5 mean very hazy skies.
AOD.why_it_matters: Tracks air pollution, dust and smoke. Falling and rising aerosols can occur in different places at once.

SOILM.label: Surface soil moisture
SOILM.definition: The amount of water held in the top 10 cm of soil, from a land surface model driven by observations. Roughly, 10 kg/m² equals 10 mm of water.
SOILM.why_it_matters: Early signal of drought stress on crops and ecosystems.

EVAP.label: Evapotranspiration
EVAP.definition: Water returned to the air from soil and open water (evaporation) plus water released by plants through their leaves (transpiration).
EVAP.why_it_matters: Links the land's water budget to heat and rainfall; irrigation and vegetation change show up here.

NDVI.label: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
NDVI.definition: A satellite measure of how green and dense plant cover is. It runs from about 0 (bare ground) to about 0.9 (dense rainforest).
NDVI.why_it_matters: Shows greening, browning, deforestation and crop change.

LST.label: Land surface temperature (day)
LST.definition: How hot the ground surface itself is at the time of the satellite pass, which is different from air temperature. Bare ground and cities can be much hotter than the air above.
LST.why_it_matters: Captures heating from land change, drying and urbanisation.
